report.summary: Chunk 2 of ollama.py: defines elision markers, window normalization, fence stripping, and window replacement validation.
risks: _CHECK_POLICY | medium | Comment claims this is weaker than deepseek.py due to missing guards for substitution and invented imports, but those guards are not in this chunk; risk of weaker safety for paid lane. | Verify that deepseek.py's additional guards (substitution, invented imports) are present in that file and not needed here.

_normalize_rewrite_windows | low | Ambiguity: bare 2-sequence at top level is interpreted as two line numbers, not (start,end). This is documented but could cause confusion. | Ensure all callers wrap ranges as [[S,E]] when intended.

_window_replacement_lines | high | Raises ValueError for elision markers but only checks if marker not in old slice; if old slice contains the marker legitimately, it might be incorrectly rejected. | Verify that legitimate markers in old slice are handled (e.g., allow if present in original).

_window_replacement_lines | medium | Requires exact line count match; if model returns same number of lines but with different line endings (e.g., missing final newline), splitlines behavior could cause mismatch. | Ensure line ending handling is robust (e.g., normalize endings before counting).

handoff.purpose: Define elision markers, window normalization, code fence stripping, and window replacement validation.

symbols.name: _ELISION_MARKERS
symbols.note: Tuple of strings that indicate elision in model output; used to reject windows containing these markers if not present in original.

symbols.name: _CHECK_POLICY
symbols.note: Dataclass replace of BASELINE_POLICY with custom elision markers; comment claims it is weaker than deepseek.py's policy.

symbols.name: _normalize_rewrite_windows
symbols.note: Normalizes window hints into sorted, merged, clamped 1-based inclusive (start, end) pairs.

symbols.name: _strip_code_fence
symbols.note: Strips markdown code fence if it wraps the entire payload.

symbols.name: _window_replacement_lines
symbols.note: Validates model-returned window and renders it with original line endings; raises ValueError on fail.

claims.text: The marker tuple stays a LOCAL literal on purpose -- see daedalus/lanes/__init__.py: it is a claim about what THIS model emits, and deepseek.py keeps its own tuple so the two lanes stay free to diverge without silently re-tuning each other.
claims.why: References daedalus/lanes/__init__.py and deepseek.py, neither present in this chunk.

claims.text: Everything else about 'is this a safe write' (truncation, parses, substitution, unresolved first-party imports) is the shared baseline, wired in below -- closing the gap measured 2026-07-30: the two guards added to deepseek.py that night (substitution, invented imports) never reached this file, so the free local default lane was strictly weaker than the paid external one for the exact two failures measured that night.

claims.text: Accepted item shapes -- all JSON-native, because the hint travels through a candidate's evidence and a task spec before it reaches this file

claims.text: A bare 2-sequence at the TOP level is therefore two line numbers, not one (start, end) -- wrap it ([[S, E]]) to mean a range.
claims.why: The function's code checks if spec is a list/tuple and iterates; a bare [S,E] would be treated as two items, each an int, resulting in two windows centered at S and E with radius.

claims.text: An unusable hint yields [], which degrades to the existing full-file behaviour. This function never invents a window.
claims.why: Function returns [] if n_lines<=0 or not spec, and if all items fail to produce valid (start,end), raw remains empty and merged remains empty.

claims.text: Drop a markdown fence wrapping the WHOLE payload. Narrow on purpose: the fence must open the first line and close the last, so a fragment that legitimately contains fenced code inside it is left alone.
claims.why: Function checks if first line starts with ``` and last line is exactly ```, then strips first and last lines; otherwise returns text unchanged.

claims.text: Raises ValueError(reason) on any fail-closed check.
claims.why: Function raises ValueError with a reason string on empty body, line count mismatch, or elision marker found.

claims.text: old_slice is the corresponding slice of splitlines(keepends=True), so the endings are available to re-attach: joining with a bare "\n" would silently convert a CRLF file and turn a two-line fix into a whole-file diff -- the opposite of what a window is for.
claims.why: The function does not show the joining logic; only validation is present in this chunk.
